title: Ecosystem
summary: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the nonliving surroundings they depend on - water, soil, sunlight, and climate - all interacting as one system. Explore how living and nonliving parts work together.

compareCandidate.label: Ecosystem vs. habitat
compareCandidate.description: A habitat is one species' home - the place that species lives in. An ecosystem is the whole system: all species PLUS the nonliving surroundings in an area.

processes: Energy flowing from sun to plants to animals
Living and nonliving depending on each other
plainLanguageExplanation: An ecosystem is everything in an area working together: all the living things (the community) plus the nonliving things around them, like water, soil, sunlight, air, and temperature. In an ecosystem, the living things depend on the nonliving parts - plants need sunlight and water, animals need plants, and decomposers recycle dead material into soil. Energy flows through the ecosystem (from sun to plants to animals), and matter is recycled. An ecosystem can be as small as a pond or a rotting log, or as large as a whole desert or forest.

whyItMatters: Ecosystems are how nature organizes life on Earth. Understanding them explains why living and nonliving things depend on each other, what happens when one part changes, and how energy and matter move through nature.
didYouKnow: A single rotting log can be a whole ecosystem, supporting fungi, insects, mosses, and bacteria that recycle its wood.
